Container.Name: OpenGym
Container.Overview: Self-hosted workout & body-weight tracker: plan routines, log workouts (supersets, warm-ups, cardio), see which muscles are trained or detrained, and import from FitNotes, Strong, or Hevy. Sign in with passkeys, a password, or your own identity provider (OIDC). Optional extras: trainers and gyms, a community library, webhooks and Strava, and an MCP server. The API, web app, and MCP server all run in this one container. Your data, your server.

Config.Name: Web UI Port
Config.Description: The published HTTP port.

Config.Name: App Data
Config.Description: Users, passkeys, session secrets, and media uploads.

Config.Name: Origin
Config.Description: The full address, scheme and port included, e.g. https://gym.example.com or http://192.168.1.1:8310. Must match the URL in the browser exactly, otherwise registrations and logins are refused due to origin mismatch.

Config.Name: Hostname
Config.Description: The application's hostname, e.g. gym.example.com (no scheme, no port). Required for passkey logins.

Config.Name: Password Login
Config.Description: Enable user password logins. If this is disabled, ensure you configure an alternative sign-in mechanism.

Config.Name: First User Is Admin
Config.Description: The first profile created on an empty instance becomes its admin. Acts only while no profile exists.

Config.Name: Allow Guest
Config.Description: Allow guest accounts to use the application. Guest data is stored in the browser.

Config.Name: Invite Only
Config.Description: Gate new profiles behind an invite code generated by an admin. Create an admin profile first before enabling this.

Config.Name: Trainers
Config.Description: Allow members to share their training with designated human coaches on the same server. Members can choose what a trainer may see or change.

Config.Name: Community Library
Config.Description: Let members share exercises, plans, sounds, and more with everyone on the server.

Config.Name: Admin UIDs
Config.Description: Comma-separated list of account IDs (Settings > Account > Account ID) that are granted access to the admin dashboard.

Config.Name: Base Path
Config.Description: Set this only for reverse proxy subpath deployments where the proxy forwards the prefix to the app. Use a leading slash and no trailing slash, e.g. /gym. Leave empty to serve at the site root.

Config.Name: OIDC Issuer
Config.Description: Single sign-on through Authentik, Authelia, Keycloak, Pocket ID or any OpenID Connect provider. Issuer URL, e.g. https://auth.example.com/application/o/opengym/. Sign-in with the provider turns on once this and OIDC Client ID are set. Register ORIGIN/api/oidc/callback as the redirect URI at the provider.

Config.Name: OIDC Client ID
Config.Description: Client ID registered at the OIDC provider.

Config.Name: OIDC Client Secret
Config.Description: Client secret from the OIDC provider. Leave empty for a public client (PKCE only).

Config.Name: OIDC Label
Config.Description: Name on the sign-in button, e.g. Authentik shows 'Sign in with Authentik.'

Config.Name: OIDC Allowed Groups
Config.Description: Comma-separated provider groups allowed to sign in, e.g. opengym. Leave empty and anyone the provider authenticates can create a profile.

Config.Name: OIDC Only
Config.Description: Make the OIDC provider the only way to sign in. Admins keep their passkeys.

Config.Name: API Tokens
Config.Description: Let each profile create scoped API tokens (Settings, API tokens) for assistants and scripts.

Config.Name: MCP Enabled
Config.Description: Run the bundled MCP server at ORIGIN/mcp, allowing AI assistants to read and change OpenGym data with a scoped API token. It also makes OpenGym the OAuth sign-in for Claude and ChatGPT connectors, which need ORIGIN to be a public HTTPS address.

Config.Name: Integrations
Config.Description: Comma-separated server-side integrations to enable: webhook (signed messages to Home Assistant, n8n, ntfy and similar when a workout is finished, a record falls, or a weigh-in is logged) and/or strava (needs STRAVA_CLIENT_ID and STRAVA_CLIENT_SECRET from your own Strava API app). Leave empty to keep them off.

Config.Name: Allow LAN
Config.Description: Let webhooks reach private network addresses (e.g. Home Assistant at http://192.168.1.20:8123). Every signed-in user can then make this server send requests into your network, so enable only if you trust everyone with an account.
